## Your Office Space: client-side fitout project management in Newcastle

Choosing an office fitout contractor in Newcastle is one part of the decision. Your business also needs a clear brief, a realistic budget, comparable proposals and someone keeping connected decisions moving on your behalf.

**Your Office Space does not undertake fitout construction as the principal contractor.** We work on the client's behalf as their project manager, coordinating the agreed brief, design, procurement and delivery process to help keep time, budget and scope on track. The appointed principal contractor and relevant trades carry out the construction work.

YOS can help organise the scope, compare proposals, coordinate the agreed project team, track decisions and variations, and report progress back to the business. The business retains its approval decisions, and the designers, contractors and certification advisers retain their respective appointed responsibilities. Our engagement scope is agreed for the actual project; project management is not a guarantee that every cost or programme risk can be eliminated.

[Explore Newcastle office fitout project management](/office-fitout) or [discuss your project with YOS](#blog-contact-form).

## What does value mean in a Newcastle office fitout?

Value means getting a suitable, usable workplace for the agreed total commitment. The lowest headline price may exclude necessary services, furniture, design work or delivery constraints. A more detailed proposal may cost more initially but make the business's remaining exposure easier to understand. Neither figure establishes value without reviewing the scope.

Start with three questions:

- **Scope:** has each contractor priced the same drawings, specifications, quantities and inclusions?
- **Budget:** which costs are fixed, provisional, excluded or still awaiting investigation?
- **Time:** what must be approved, ordered or made available before the proposed programme can start?

For early budget planning, read our [Newcastle commercial fitout cost guide](/blog/commercial-fitout-cost-newcastle-2026). This article focuses on contractor selection and comparison, rather than introducing another generic square-metre price range.

## How this Newcastle fitout contractor guide was selected

This guide is published by Your Office Space, which offers client-side project management and workplace services. The following 15 businesses are listed alphabetically for navigation only, with no ranking or order of preference. The selection draws on published fitout services, a Newcastle service presence or documented Newcastle projects, reviewed on 18 November 2026.

Some firms are local specialists; others serve Newcastle through a regional or national business. Their appointment models and construction scopes can differ. Inclusion is not an independent quality award, a recommendation for every project or a claim that YOS has worked with each provider. This is a selected guide, not a complete register of every contractor operating in the region.

The profiles describe published capabilities. We have not obtained comparable live tenders, independently tested workmanship or verified every firm's current capacity, insurance or applicable licences. Confirm the contracting entity, relevant credentials, proposed team, availability and terms for your own project.

## Newcastle office and commercial fitout contractors to consider

### Built

**Published focus: National construction resources with a Newcastle office.**

Built combines a Newcastle office with a national construction business. Its own published project announcements include the Coal LSL office fitout. This gives readers a broader construction and refurbishment option alongside dedicated local interiors firms.

**A useful question:** Ask which local team would deliver your project, what scale of work it is currently considering and how preconstruction, design coordination and delivery are proposed.

[View Built's published information](https://www.built.com.au/locations/).

### CIProjects

**Published focus: Fitout, refurbishment and make-good services.**

CIProjects publishes a Newcastle service offering covering commercial fitouts, refurbishments, upgrades and make-good work. Its stated scope brings together several stages of a tenancy change, which may be relevant when the old and new workplaces need coordinated work.

**A useful question:** Ask for separate scopes and programmes for the new fitout, existing-premises make-good and any building upgrades.

[View CIProjects's published information](https://www.ciprojects.com.au/locations/newcastle-fitout/).

### Core Project Group

**Published focus: Documented Newcastle corporate-office projects.**

Core Project Group is credited as the builder for the 727HQ Newcastle office fitout in the polytec Design Awards project record. Its published portfolio also identifies Newcastle workplace projects. These provide specific local examples to discuss when assessing comparable experience.

**A useful question:** Ask for current examples that match your building condition and fitout complexity, and confirm the proposed construction team.

[View Core Project Group's published information](https://www.polytecdesignawards.com.au/projects/2024/1937/).

### Evoke Projects

**Published focus: Workplace strategy with healthcare and office design experience.**

Evoke publishes a Newcastle office presence and combines workplace strategy, design and fitout services. Its local offering includes offices, medical practices, dental clinics and veterinary facilities, giving it a stated focus on both workplace and clinical environments.

**A useful question:** Ask how workflow, privacy, equipment and specialist services requirements would be resolved in the design and construction scope.

[View Evoke Projects's published information](https://evokeprojects.com.au/location/fitouts-newcastle/).

### Graph Building

**Published focus: Fitout alongside broader commercial construction.**

Graph publishes office-building and fitout projects within a wider commercial construction portfolio. Its stated experience includes refurbishment and extensions, sometimes around continuing operations or within heritage buildings. This is a different delivery profile from a furniture-only or light-refresh supplier.

**A useful question:** Ask how building alterations, existing conditions and occupied-site constraints would be investigated and priced.

[View Graph Building's published information](https://graph.com.au/projects/).

### Graphite Projects

**Published focus: Complex workplace refurbishment and early contractor involvement.**

Graphite is a fitout and refurbishment head contractor with documented Newcastle work. Its City of Newcastle project involved multiple floors, office and call-centre accommodation, council chambers and coordinated building services under an early contractor involvement and construction management arrangement.

**A useful question:** Ask which procurement model suits the project and how early design development, cost advice and construction responsibilities would be documented.

[View Graphite Projects's published information](https://www.graphiteprojects.com.au/portfolio-item/city-of-newcastle/).

### Insight Building Services

**Published focus: Hunter-based fitout and commercial building capability.**

Insight describes a Hunter-based commercial construction offering spanning fitouts, medical projects, building refurbishments and new construction. Its published services cover both interior works and broader building projects across Newcastle and the surrounding region.

**A useful question:** Ask how the proposal separates the fitout scope from any base-building upgrades or investigations still required.

[View Insight Building Services's published information](https://www.insightbuildingservices.com.au/).

### JG Building

**Published focus: Office, retail, hospitality and showroom fitouts.**

JG Building promotes commercial fitouts across Newcastle, Lake Macquarie and the Hunter, with planning, design, construction and handover within its published offering. Its stated range includes offices, retail spaces, hospitality venues and showrooms.

**A useful question:** Ask for relevant examples in your business sector and a written explanation of what is included from design through handover.

[View JG Building's published information](https://jgbuild.com.au/commercial-fitouts/).

### Kingston Building

**Published focus: Commercial construction with in-house design management.**

Kingston publishes commercial fitout capability across offices, industrial and manufacturing premises, retail, healthcare and education. It describes an in-house design manager and the ability to work from existing architectural plans or help develop the design.

**A useful question:** Ask how design responsibilities, services coordination and construction pricing will be allocated for your particular brief.

[View Kingston Building's published information](https://kingstonbuilding.com.au/services/commercial-fit-outs/).

### Newcastle Office Interiors

**Published focus: Office fitout, refurbishment and furniture coordination.**

Newcastle Office Interiors combines office fitout and refurbishment with furniture and data/electrical services. It identifies professional services and defence contractors as areas of specialisation, including knowledge of defence-related requirements and zoning.

**A useful question:** Ask which requirements apply to your organisation and how the furniture, services and construction packages would be coordinated.

[View Newcastle Office Interiors's published information](https://www.newcastleofficeinteriors.com.au/).

### North Construction & Building

**Published focus: Regional construction presence and a fitout/refurbishment portfolio.**

North maintains a regional construction presence including Newcastle and publishes a dedicated fitout and refurbishment portfolio. Its work extends across commercial and institutional environments, giving readers another option where interior works connect with broader construction requirements.

**A useful question:** Ask for comparable workplace projects and confirm the team, scope and procurement arrangement proposed for your site.

[View North Construction & Building's published information](https://www.north.com.au/projects-fitout-refurb/).

### Radford Shopfitters

**Published focus: Commercial joinery and bespoke shopfitting.**

Radford publishes office fitout and commercial joinery services alongside medical, hospitality and retail shopfitting. Its offering includes planning, project management and production, with bespoke joinery a prominent part of its stated capability.

**A useful question:** Ask which joinery items are included, how finishes and samples are approved and how manufacturing dates connect to installation.

[View Radford Shopfitters's published information](https://radfordshopfitters.com.au/).

### SHAPE Newcastle

**Published focus: Local team backed by national fitout resources.**

SHAPE has a dedicated Newcastle office and publishes local corporate-office, education and refurbishment projects. Its Newcastle portfolio includes projects for Allianz and Hall & Wilcox, alongside University of Newcastle work.

**A useful question:** Ask for relevant local references and clarify the proposed delivery model, project team and management of an occupied building.

[View SHAPE Newcastle's published information](https://shape.com.au/location/newcastle/).

### Skelcon

**Published focus: Integrated design, construction and joinery.**

Skelcon presents a Newcastle-based design and construction offering across commercial, medical and hospitality projects. Its Ramboll Newcastle project describes coordination between its design, construction and joinery departments for an office fitout.

**A useful question:** Ask whether your brief is best suited to an integrated design-and-construct appointment or a separately developed design.

[View Skelcon's published information](https://skelcon.com.au/projects/ramboll-newcastle).

### Total Fitouts Newcastle

**Published focus: Local operators supported by a wider fitout network.**

Total Fitouts Newcastle promotes a locally operated team within the wider Total Fitouts network. Its published commercial design and fitout offering spans offices, retail, hospitality, medical, fitness, wellness and display suites.

**A useful question:** Ask who holds the project appointment, which local team will deliver it and what the design, construction and handover proposal includes.

[View Total Fitouts Newcastle's published information](https://www.totalfitouts.com.au/location/shop-fitouts-newcastle/).

## Compare contractors using one project brief

Before asking several businesses for a price, prepare one consistent pack. A contractor can only price the information it receives, and missing decisions tend to reappear later as assumptions, allowances or changes.

Include the premises address, measured layout, intended use, room requirements, existing conditions and target occupation date. Record landlord works, retained furniture and equipment, working-hour restrictions and whether the business needs to keep operating during the project. Give every tenderer the same information revision and record subsequent clarifications.

Use our [Newcastle fitout planning checklist](/blog/office-fitout-newcastle-planning-checklist) to organise the brief, then keep this contractor guide beside the proposals you receive.

## Ask these questions before comparing the totals

| Comparison point | What to ask | Why it affects value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Design and investigations | Who measures, designs and investigates the existing building and services? | Missing investigations leave important pricing assumptions unresolved. |
| Construction scope | Are partitions, finishes, joinery and services priced against the same documents? | Similar descriptions can conceal different quantities or specifications. |
| Mechanical, power and data | What existing capacity is assumed and which alterations are included? | Services requirements can materially change the budget. |
| Furniture and equipment | What is supplied, installed, reused or provided by others? | A construction price may not include a functioning furnished workplace. |
| Access and staging | What working hours, loading, occupied areas and site restrictions have been allowed for? | Access conditions affect sequencing, disruption and delivery costs. |
| Allowances and exclusions | Which items remain provisional, excluded or subject to investigation? | The headline quote may leave additional costs with the client. |
| Programme | What starts the clock and which client decisions or purchases are dependencies? | An unqualified number of weeks is difficult to compare. |
| Variations and handover | How are changes approved and what completion records will be supplied? | Clear decisions and completion criteria help control scope and outstanding work. |

A contractor's website can help establish whether there is relevant experience to discuss. It cannot establish the final price, suitability or appointment terms for your project.

[Download the existing office construction quote comparison worksheet (TXT)](/guides/office-construction-quote-comparison-newcastle.txt). It provides a place to record scope, exclusions, allowances, dependencies and unresolved decisions without requiring an email address. For a worked comparison example, use our [Newcastle office construction quote guide](/blog/compare-office-construction-quotes-newcastle).

## Practical tips for choosing your Newcastle fitout builder

### Match the builder to the job you actually have

A contractor's best-looking project may not resemble yours. Ask about work with a similar building condition, intended use, services complexity and operating constraints. A refurbishment in an occupied office raises different questions from fitting out an empty tenancy.

**Useful tip:** give shortlisted contractors the same one-page project summary before requesting proposals. Ask each to explain where its experience fits the brief and which parts would need specialist input.

### Ask who will be on your project, not only who wins the work

Find out who will estimate the job, lead construction, coordinate design information and communicate with your business. Ask how often you should expect updates and who makes decisions when the usual contact is unavailable. Confirm availability for the actual project instead of treating a website enquiry as a reserved start date.

**Useful tip:** ask to meet the proposed delivery lead before appointment and record the agreed communication and escalation process.

### Speak with relevant past clients

Request references for comparable work, with the reference client's permission. Ask about communication, treatment of changes, management of occupied premises and how outstanding items were resolved. A photograph shows the finished appearance; a reference conversation can help you understand how the process worked.

**Useful tip:** ask what information the client wishes they had prepared earlier. This can reveal practical briefing gaps without turning the conversation into a search for complaints.

### Test the exclusions before negotiating the headline price

Invite each contractor to identify what it has assumed, excluded or left provisional. Check design, approvals, services, furniture, IT, protection of existing areas, waste removal and handover information. Ask for any cost-saving alternative to show what changes in specification, scope or performance.

**Useful tip:** ask, “What will our business still need to arrange or pay for to make this workplace ready to use?” Record each answer against an owner and a budget line.

### Check credentials and appointment terms for the actual work

Confirm the contracting entity, relevant insurance and the credentials applicable to the proposed work. Use [Service NSW's builder and tradesperson licence check](https://www.service.nsw.gov.au/transaction/check-a-builder-or-tradesperson-licence) where applicable, and ask the relevant advisers about requirements you are unsure of. A company name, logo or membership badge does not establish every credential required for your project.

Have your solicitor and relevant advisers review the proposed appointment, payment terms, change process, completion obligations and allocation of responsibilities before commitment. Do not assume another company's contract is suitable for your business.

### Resolve unclear answers before signing

Pause to clarify proposals that do not identify the information priced, contain unexplained allowances, promise a start without confirming prerequisites or leave the change-approval process unclear. These are questions to resolve, not proof that a contractor is unsuitable.

**Useful tip:** keep one written clarification register. Share relevant scope clarifications consistently with the shortlisted contractors so the comparison remains fair.

## Manage the fitout yourself or appoint a client-side project manager?

Here, **DIY means the business coordinates its own project**. It does not mean undertaking building, electrical, plumbing or other specialist work yourself. The appointed contractors and specialist advisers still carry out their respective work, and responsibilities must be confirmed in their appointments.

A capable owner or internal facilities lead may manage a clearly defined project successfully. A client-side project manager can be useful when the brief is evolving, several providers need coordination or senior people cannot give the project sustained attention. Neither approach removes the need for an appropriate principal contractor, design advice or other required appointments.

| Decision | Business manages the project directly | Client-side project manager engaged |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Brief and scope | Your nominated internal lead gathers requirements and maintains the agreed scope. | The PM helps organise the brief, interfaces and scope decisions within the engagement. |
| Comparing proposals | Your team reconciles inclusions, exclusions, assumptions and open questions. | The PM helps structure the comparison and brings unresolved decisions to the client. |
| Time commitment | Allow time for meetings, clarifications, approvals, records and follow-up alongside normal business duties. | Allow time for client approvals and decisions, with agreed coordination and reporting handled by the PM. |
| Budget control | Your team maintains the cost plan, commitments, allowances and change register. | The PM helps track and report the agreed cost information and proposed changes; the client retains spending approvals. |
| Programme | Your team connects client decisions, design information, procurement and the contractor's programme. | The PM helps coordinate these dependencies and escalates issues within the agreed role. |
| Construction delivery | The appointed principal contractor and trades perform and manage their contracted construction work. | The appointed principal contractor and trades continue to perform and manage their contracted construction work. |
| Cost of coordination | Consider internal staff time, any external advice and the effect on day-to-day operations. | Include the PM fee and its scope, alongside the client time and specialist advice still required. |

### When managing it internally may be a reasonable option

- The scope is well defined and the key design and building questions have been resolved.
- One internal lead has relevant experience, authority and genuine time available.
- The business can maintain a consistent brief, cost record, decision register and communication process.
- The interfaces between the landlord, designer, builder, furniture supplier and other providers are understood.
- The internal team knows when to seek specialist advice rather than making an unsupported decision.

A small floor area alone does not make a project simple. Services changes, specialist use, occupied premises or tight lease dates can create substantial coordination demands in a modest tenancy.

### When client-side project management may add value

- You are comparing premises or proposals with different scope assumptions.
- The design, services, furniture and occupation plans need to be developed together.
- Several providers need information or decisions from one another.
- The business must continue operating while work takes place.
- Senior people need to stay focused on customers and operations.
- You want a structured client-side record of costs, decisions, changes and programme dependencies.

Ask a prospective PM to define deliverables, reporting, decision authority, fees and exclusions. Confirm how the role differs from the builder's project manager and which responsibilities remain with your business and other appointed providers.

### Compare the full business commitment

A fair comparison includes the PM's fee, your internal time under either approach, other adviser costs and the project's coordination needs. Do not assume a PM will automatically recover its fee through construction savings or eliminate delays. Equally, treating an owner's time as free can hide a significant business commitment.

**Useful tip:** list the decisions expected over the next month, nominate who would manage them internally and estimate the time they can realistically allocate. Use that discussion to decide whether external client-side support would be useful for the actual project.

YOS can discuss an agreed client-side role for your Newcastle fitout. We do not take on the principal contractor's construction role, and the engagement should make the division of responsibilities clear. [Discuss the coordination support your project needs](#blog-contact-form).

## Why square-metre prices need a scope check

A fitout rate per square metre is only useful when you understand what sits inside it. Furniture, mechanical upgrades, joinery, professional fees and existing-building conditions can change the total substantially without changing the floor area.

Use a rate as an early planning guide, then develop the design and budget together. Ask for the construction total, other project costs, unpriced items and assumptions to be shown separately. Confirm GST treatment so proposals can be compared on the same basis.

Our [fitout estimator](/resources/fitout-estimator) is an indicative planning tool, not a contractor tender or a confirmed Newcastle construction price. The actual business case needs the premises, design, services investigations and current project-specific quotes.

## Keep time, budget and scope connected

A finish change can affect both cost and procurement. A room-layout change can affect furniture, mechanical services and data. A delayed client decision can affect when a contractor can proceed. These interfaces need a clear owner and a written record.

Under an agreed client-side engagement, YOS helps coordinate the project information, report costs and programme dependencies, track proposed changes and bring decisions back to the client. This supports the appointed contractor's delivery process while keeping the business's requirements visible.

[Watch our fitout project management guide](/videos/office-fitout-project-management) for an explanation of decision ownership. For the distinction between appointments, read [client-side project manager versus builder](/blog/commercial-construction-project-manager-vs-builder-newcastle).

## Common questions

### Which Newcastle fitout contractor offers the best value?

The best value depends on the premises, scope, design, specification and delivery requirements. Compare current proposals against one consistent brief, including allowances, exclusions, programme dependencies and handover obligations. This guide does not rank contractors or identify a universally cheapest provider.

### Does Your Office Space build office fitouts as principal contractor?

No. YOS provides client-side project management under an agreed engagement. We help coordinate the brief, budget, scope and programme on the client’s behalf. The appointed principal contractor and relevant trades carry out the construction work.

### Should I compare office fitout quotes by price per square metre?

Use square-metre pricing as an early guide only. Check the included scope and compare construction, furniture, services upgrades, professional fees and unpriced items separately. Develop the design and business-case budget together before commitment.

### Are the contractors listed in order of preference?

No. The 15 contractors are listed alphabetically for navigation, with no ranking or order of preference. Profiles summarise published capabilities and do not establish current capacity, verified credentials or suitability for a particular project.

### Can my Newcastle fitout business be added?

Contact the YOS Furniture team with your business name, website, Newcastle coverage and relevant project examples. We can review your business for a future update and discuss furniture supply opportunities separately. Inclusion does not require a purchase.


### Can our business manage its own office fitout?

Yes, a business can coordinate its own project when it has the relevant capability, time and clear appointments. DIY coordination does not mean carrying out construction or specialist trade work yourself. Assess the scope, services, operating constraints and time commitment before choosing the approach.

### What is the difference between a builder’s project manager and a client-side project manager?

The builder’s project manager manages delivery within the builder’s appointment. A client-side project manager works under an appointment from the client to coordinate agreed information, costs, decisions and programme interfaces on the client’s behalf. Confirm the actual authority, deliverables and responsibilities in each engagement.
